correctness.rationale: The standard Minkowski sum gives total coordinate sum M and exact tube offsets \(z(T)=(2^a-1)(2^b-1)\). All singleton facets have offset zero and intrinsic normal norm \(\sqrt{(N-1)/N}\); summing their ball constraints yields the sharp radius upper bound and forces the unique uniform center at equality. For every connected proper tube, the coordinatewise monotonicity of \(F(r,s)=((2^r-1)(2^s-1))/((r+s)(r+s-1))\) yields a strict support-density bound. After division by the exact projected subset-normal norm, every non-singleton tube is strictly farther than the singleton radius. Thus the displayed ball is feasible, optimal, uniquely centered, and tangent exactly to singleton facets.

value.rationale: Complete bipartite graph associahedra are a named and actively studied graph-associahedron family with dedicated diameter results, but their standard realization has exponentially many connected-subset facets. The theorem identifies a canonical Euclidean size invariant for every genuine biclique and proves a strong structural collapse: only \(p+q\) singleton facets control the largest ball among \(p+q+(2^p-1)(2^q-1)-1\) facets. The exact formula interpolates a genuinely two-parameter family and requires a new monotonicity comparison absent from the star boundary case, so it is not merely a routine restatement of the stellohedron result.
